intervention_scopes: Reduce earned advance release from eight to four while keeping stated goods cost and cash fixed: income falls four and liability rises four.
Remove the inventory write-down: book inventory/income rise six but neither CFO nor usable cash changes.
An extra inception outlay of 29/4, explicitly paid from the investor's retained ten, exhausts the project surplus; value and resources change together.
Physical probabilities 1/3, 2/5 and 3/5 move the unique log optimum to zero, one-quarter and one, with traded Arrow prices unchanged.
Halve the year-one contribution to forty and recompute final wealth as 144: the time-weighted return stays eight percent while annual IRR becomes positive.
Increase the monitored haircut just above 3/11: the original hedge's payoff still matches but its original debt/share positions are inadmissible.
An up-node one-third haircut requires delivered equity 50/11 with the entire five-unit terminal residual; a smaller or unexecuted contribution leaves the financing gap.
Reduce the lender's separate reserve from sixty to fifty: inception still funds, but the required up-node second advance cannot be executed.
Compare original, minimum upstream and minimum direct grants, retaining all nominal claims and unused donor cash; the extra upstream half-unit reaches other creditors.
Redirect half of the minimal upstream outlay from A to B: total donor cash is unchanged but T misses its deadline.
Expand the donor budget and grant eight to A: A hits its face cap and retains one, so the original uncapped formulas cannot be extrapolated.
